blocks.tamil_translation: will be accepted. When the sun rises from the west, a seal will be placed on the hearts in whatever state each person's heart is in (Iman or kufr). The deeds that people did before this alone (will be sufficient for their everlasting success or everlasting failure).” Hazrat Mu'awiyah, Hazrat Abdur Rahman ibn Awf and Hazrat Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As (RA) have narrated that Rasulullah ﷺ said this.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو ﵄ قَالَ: قَالَ رَجُلٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ! أَيُّ الْهِجْرَةِ أَفْضَلُ؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تَهْجُرَ مَا كَرِهَ رَبُّكَ وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: اَلْهِجْرَةُ هِجْرَتَانِ هِجْرَةُ الْحَاضِرِ وَهِجْرَةُ الْبَادِي، فَأَمَّا الْبَادِي فَيُجِيبُ إِذَا دُعِيَ وَيُطِيعُ إِذَا أُمِرَ، وَأَمَّا الْحَاضِرُ فَهُوَ أَعْظَمُهُمَا بَلِيَّةً وَأَعْظَمُهُمَا أَجْرًا.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه النسائي باب هجرة البادي، رقم:٤١٧٠
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) narrates, “O Rasulullah, which is the best of Hijrahs?” a man asked. “That you leave the deeds that your Lord dislikes,” he replied. “Hijrah is of two kinds: 1. the Hijrah of the town-dweller, 2. the Hijrah of the villager. The Hijrah of the one who lives in a village is that when he is called (away from his place) he comes, and when he is given some command he obeys it. (The Hijrah of the one who lives in a town is also the same.) However, their Hijrah involves a greater trial, and its reward is also greater.

blocks.text: Explanation:- The town-dweller leaves his possessions, his goods and many tasks behind and goes out in the path of Allah Ta'ala. Therefore his making Hijrah (migrating) in the path of Allah Ta'ala is a great trial, and so it becomes a cause of receiving a greater reward.
